dedupe_keys.name: keysight exata and qualnet network modeling

description: EXata and QualNet are commercial network modelling tools that build a network digital twin of an entire communication network, with its protocol layers, radios, antennas and devices. QualNet is the simulator: it uses parallel discrete-event simulation to run large networks of thousands of nodes faster than real time, and models wired, wireless, underwater and satellite networks, cellular standards from GSM to LTE and 5G, and military waveforms such as Link-11 and Link-16, with terrain, propagation and mobility models, a post-simulation analyser, SQL statistics and signal heat maps. EXata adds real-time emulation, representing the network as a software virtual network that interoperates with real radios and devices for hardware-in-the-loop and cyber testing. Both were developed by Scalable Network Technologies and are now sold by Keysight Technologies. Coverage: user-built scenarios placed on real terrain anywhere; no network data is supplied. Format and access: licensed desktop and server software with a GUI and human-in-the-loop interface, VR-Link for HLA and DIS federation; paid, with prices on request. Caveats: proprietary and costly; Keysight's website blocks automated readers, so details here come from the QualNet technical overview. Simulation uses: resilience and cascading-failure analysis of communication networks under attack or outage, capacity planning, emergency and defence communications, and network digital twins. Related records: NetSim and Riverbed Modeler are commercial peers, ns-3 and OMNeT++ are open alternatives, and STK can be coupled for space links.
